input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Spirit Airlines

output.company: Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. (parent of Spirit Airlines, LLC) – 'Spirit Airlines'

financials.stated_by: Company plan presented in court, reported by CNBC

credit_ratings.summary: Moody's cut its overall corporate rating to Caa3 from Caa1, two notches. It cited cash burn of more than $500m expected in 2025 and noted the $275m revolver was fully drawn.

Fitch cut its long-term issuer rating to 'D' (default) from 'CCC-' after the second Chapter 11 filing. Secured debt at Spirit IP Cayman and Spirit Loyalty Cayman was cut to 'C' with expected average recovery (RR4). Fitch called liquidation risk 'elevated'. The date is the publication date of the report.
I could not confirm any S&P action after the second filing, or any rating action after the May 2026 shutdown. The ratings are effectively at default or no longer meaningful.

debt_events.summary: Emerged from the first Chapter 11 case, filed in November 2024.
Fully drew the $275m exit revolver, which matures 2028-03-12.
Filed a second Chapter 11 case: In re Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc., No. 25-11897 (SHL), Bankruptcy Court, Southern District of New York. Six related companies are debtors.
Signed a bankruptcy loan agreement for up to $475m of new money term loans, drawn in installments. The 10-K also describes a deal with AerCap that provides about $150m of cash.

Signed a restructuring agreement with creditors. It would use $150m of pledged cash to repay part of the bankruptcy loan, pay $100m when the plan took effect, and give new equity mainly to the bankruptcy-loan lenders.

Announced an orderly wind-down and cancelled all flights. The company said no further funding was available after fuel prices rose sharply and that it needed 'hundreds of millions of additional dollars of liquidity'. Vouchers, credits and loyalty points are left to be settled in the bankruptcy.
The court approved the wind-down. On 2026-05-27 the company filed sale procedures for its LaGuardia slots, headquarters campus, Free Spirit loyalty program, spare engines, simulators and equipment.

Asset sales: JetBlue won the 22 LaGuardia slots for $58.5m, subject to court and FAA approval. Wayne County Airport Authority agreed to pay $18m for the Detroit hangar lease. A $533.5m opening bid covered about 20 aircraft plus the loyalty program.

payment_behaviour.summary: Former employees filed a proposed class action covering about 17,000 workers. It alleges Spirit broke the WARN Act by ending jobs without 60 days' notice and seeks 60 days of wages and benefits.
Customer vouchers, credits and Free Spirit points were not honoured. How they are treated was left to the bankruptcy process.

distress_signals.summary: The FY2025 10-K says there is 'substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern'. Active employees fell to 7,482 from 11,331 a year earlier. The stock was delisted from NYSE American and trades on OTC Pink as FLYYQ.

Flights stopped and nearly all staff lost their jobs. Talks on a proposed $500m federal rescue stalled, and no airline was willing to buy Spirit. Jet fuel reached about $4.51/gal, against $2.24 assumed in the plan.
Deal talks with Castlelake and Frontier produced no transaction. The plan relied on shrinking the fleet and network.

ownership.value: Public company (stock trades on OTC Pink as FLYYQ after NYSE American delisting). The prior equity was replaced by creditor-owned equity at the March 2025 bankruptcy exit. The company is now a Chapter 11 debtor being wound down under court supervision. The wind-down release names its main financial stakeholders as Citadel, Cyrus Capital and Ares Management.

output.risk_rationale: Spirit Aviation Holdings filed its second Chapter 11 case on 2025-08-29, only five months after leaving the first one. It stopped all flights and began an orderly wind-down on 2026-05-02 after its creditor-backed plan failed when fuel prices spiked and no rescue was found. Assets such as the LaGuardia slots, aircraft, Detroit hangar and loyalty program are being sold. Fitch rates it 'D' and Moody's last rated it Caa3, the 10-K carries going-concern doubt, and about 17,000 laid-off workers are suing over the WARN Act. The company has no operating business left: recovery for any counterparty depends on the bankruptcy waterfall, and unsecured trade claims should be treated as largely impaired.
